summary.headline: Orders and revenue both finished the week ahead of target, but the quarter is still at 90.0% of target with four weeks to go.

points.what: Orders reached 817, or 101.2% of the weekly target, and revenue reached $62,651, or 108.7% of target.
points.so_what: Revenue ran further ahead of target than orders, so the beat came from order value as well as order volume.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue of $477,960 stands at 90.0% of the target for the same weeks, a gap of $53,400.
points.so_what: A single week ahead of target does not change the quarter position, which remains behind.

points.what: Orders grew 62.1% and revenue 64.7% against the same week last year, while the targets assume 75% growth.
points.so_what: Growth is running under the pace the targets were built on, which is how a week can beat target while the year stays behind.

points.what: New customer signups fell 10.8% week on week to 256, a notable move rated bad, while orders rose 3.5%.
points.so_what: Signups were the one measure moving the wrong way in a week when the order and revenue targets were met.

points.what: The quarter is behind at 90.0% of target, with $296,595 still needed against the full quarter target of $774,555 in the four weeks left.
points.so_what: Reaching the quarter target would require weekly revenue well above the level of recent weeks.

points.what: Year-to-date revenue is at 90.0% of target, and the rest of the year needs $77,519 a week against a recent eight-week run-rate of $53,830.
points.so_what: At the current pace the full-year target of $3,888,802 is out of reach.

points.what: Signups are up 9.9% on last year while orders are up 62.1%.
points.so_what: Customer growth is running far below order growth, and that gap is the main thing to watch behind an otherwise on-target week.

points.what: Orders came in at 101.2% of the weekly target and revenue at 108.7%, both ahead, against next week's targets of 838 orders and $58,985.
points.so_what: The week cleared both targets, which is the first requirement for narrowing the shortfall built up this quarter.

points.what: Quarter-to-date revenue is 90.0% of target, $53,400 behind, with $296,595 left to reach the full quarter target in four weeks.
points.so_what: The shortfall is large enough that beats of this week's size do not close it.

points.what: Year-to-date attainment is 90.0%, with January at 88.0% and February at 92.4% of target.
points.so_what: Every completed month so far has landed behind target, so the year starts from a deficit rather than a cushion.

points.what: LATAM orders rose 25.2% to 134, contributing 27 orders, or 96.4% of the weekly change.
points.so_what: Almost all of the weekly order gain sits in the smallest region, giving the increase a narrow base.

points.what: Search orders rose 4.7% to 575, contributing 26 orders, or 92.9% of the weekly change, and hold a 70.4% share.
points.so_what: Movement in the largest source carries far more weight for target attainment than swings in the small sources.

points.what: Facebook orders fell 27.3% to 48, a contribution of -18 orders, while EMEA orders fell 4.9% to 156.
points.so_what: These declines offset part of what LATAM and Search added, holding the net order gain to a modest step up.

points.what: AOV rose 7.2% week on week to $89.50 but remains 1.2% below the same week last year, rated bad.
points.so_what: With order value still under last year, the year-on-year revenue gain rests on order volume.

points.what: The cancellation rate fell 4.7 pp to 14.3%, a notable move rated good, and sits below last year's 16.7%.
points.so_what: At $731 of revenue per percentage point of cancellations, the lower rate worked in favour of this week's revenue attainment.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 09 Feb 2026 was flat at 10.8%, 1.5 pp above last year, rated bad.
points.so_what: Returns running above last year works against the value of what was sold, since gross revenue does not subtract them.

checks.name: 14-Day Return Rate names its mature week
anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
each slot only covers its allowed KPIs
